texts.preamble: Gurlal Alias Baggi vs State Of U.P. on 22 September, 2020 Author: Siddharth Bench: Siddharth High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 70 Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 19639 of 2020 Applicant :- Gurlal Alias Baggi
texts.arguments: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. Submission is that Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been enacted by the legislature and hence the implication of the applicant under section 272, 273 I.P.C. is unjustified. Offence under section 60(1) of Excise Act is bailable and triable by Magistrate. False recovery has been alleged. The applicant is languishing in jail since 5.2.2020.The criminal history of eight cases of the applicant has been explained in paragraph-2 and 3 of the supplementary affidavit. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant but could not dispute the aforesaid fact.. Gurlal Alias Baggi vs State Of U.P. on 22 September, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2967143/ 1 Keeping in view the nature of the offence, argument advanced on behalf of the parties, spreading of novel corona virus in jails, evidence on record regarding complicity of the accused, larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Dataram Singh Vs. State of U.P. and another reported in (2018)3 SCC 22 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
